- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.1) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.8), model underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid missing downward momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30d horizon (first 5–7 days); apply +0.3–0.8% bias to first 5 days.
- After sharp price spikes (≥+3% from prior 5-day avg), model overreacts and forecasts overshoot; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak for next 3 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +1.2, -0.5, +1.1), model fails to capture mean reversion; apply -0.2% to forecast 3–5 days after sentiment shifts from positive to neutral/negative.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome exceeds model by >2.5% in 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 0.5% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is flat (±0.1–0.3) for 3+ days, model drifts toward historical mean; apply -0.3% to forecast to avoid overconfidence bias.
